div.l: Who so be rebell to my Iugement
Shal pai for al that bi þe wei is spent
Now draw cut or we forþer twyn̄
He which hath þe shortest shal begyn̄
Sir knight qduod he my maist̉er and lorde
Now draweth kut for it is myn Accorde
Come ner͗e qduod he my ladi prioresse
And ye ʆsir Clerk late be youre shamefastnesse
Ne studith not ley hond on eueri man̄
And anone to draw iche wight began̄
And shortli to tel as it was
Were it be auenture sort or caas
The sothe is · þe cut fel to þe kniȝt
Of which ful glad was eueri wight
And tel most his tale as was resoıı̄un
Be forward and composicoıı̄un
And ye haue herd what nedeth wordez mo
And whan þis good sagh that it was so
As he þat wise was and obedient
Toke his forward be his owne assent
He seid sethens I shal begin þe game
Welcom be þe cut in goddꝭes name
Now late vs ride and herkeneth what I say
And with that worde we riden forth oure wey
Here beginneth the knightes tale
Whilom as old stories tellen vs
There was a duke þat hight Thesius
Of Athenes he was lorde and gouernoure
And in his tyme suche a conqueroure
That gretter was none vnder þe son
Ful many a riche contre had he won
What with his wisdome and chivalri
He conquered al þe regne of femyny
That whilom was called Cithia
And wedded þe quene Ipolita
And brought hir home into his contre
With moche merth and solempnite
And eke hir͗e yong suster Emely
And þus with victori and melody
Lete I this noble Duke ride
And his host in armes be his side
And certes if it ner to long to her͗e
I wold haue told you fullich þe mater͗e
